intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and international delicacies. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients used in authentic Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food Experience
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a local roadside market to try tlayudas, tamales, and pulque, a traditional fermented agave drink.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from CDMX)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the bohemian cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan crafts at the local market, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a family-run fondita serving mole and chiles en nogada.

experiences.name: Roma & Condesa Taco Crawl
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided evening taco crawl through the trendy Roma and Condesa neighborhoods. Sample tacos al pastor, suadero, and barbacoa from legendary street stands, wash them down with agua fresca, and soak in the vibrant local nightlife atmosphere.

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walking Tour
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior of the Palacio de Bellas Artes, explore the Diego Rivera murals inside, then walk through the historic Zócalo square, visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, and discover the ruins of the Templo Mayor, the ancient Aztec ceremonial center.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up, then take a leisurely walk to explore the immediate neighborhood. Head to the nearby Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world — completely free to visit. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace from the outside.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the historic centro streets, browse street vendors, and soak in the atmosphere of the city at dusk. Visit the lit-up Zócalo for a memorable first evening view.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack at the airport before landing or skip — meal plan starts at lunch.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan or a nearby taquería in Centro Histórico — tacos al pastor or quesadillas for under 80 MXN (~$4 USD).
meals.dinner: El Huequito (famous for tacos de pastor) in Centro Histórico — budget-friendly, authentic, and beloved by locals. Expect to spend 100–150 MXN (~$5–8 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts after 13:00 arrival. Use the Metro (Line 2, Zócalo station) for cheap transport — single ride costs about 5 MXN. Get a rechargeable Metro card at the airport or station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum — one of the most important Aztec ruins in Mexico, located steps from the Zócalo. Entry is about 85 MXN (~$4 USD). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and museum exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau exterior and the murals inside by Diego Rivera — entry to the main hall is free. Afterward, explore Alameda Central park, a beautiful public green space ideal for people-watching and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) nearby or explore the street food scene around Eje Central. Enjoy the vibrant nighttime energy of the centro.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole from a street cart near the hotel — a classic Mexico City breakfast for under 50 MXN (~$2.50 USD).
meals.lunch: Tortas at a local torta shop near Alameda Central — hearty sandwiches for 60–90 MXN (~$3–4.50 USD).
meals.dinner: Mercado de San Juan evening stalls or a local comida corrida (set meal) restaurant — 3-course meal for 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with the Chapultepec visit. Carry small change for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Chapultepec (Line 1, Chapultepec station). Explore Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the world — free entry. Visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum) for 85 MXN (~$4 USD) and enjoy panoramic views of the city from the hilltop castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby — window-shop along Presidente Masaryk Avenue and enjoy free street art and architecture. Head back toward Roma or Condesa neighborhoods via Metro or a short walk for a more bohemian, local vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Colonia Roma on foot — browse independent bookshops, cafés, and street murals. This neighborhood has a fantastic food and culture scene beloved by locals.

meals.breakfast: Chilaquiles at a local breakfast spot in Centro — a filling traditional dish for 70–100 MXN (~$3.50–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Street food in Chapultepec park — elotes (corn on the cob) and tlayudas from vendors for under 60 MXN (~$3 USD).
meals.dinner: Tacos de canasta or gorditas at a street stall in Colonia Roma — dinner for under 100 MXN (~$5 USD). Try Taquería Los Cocuyos if nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — Chapultepec park is large and involves walking on uneven terrain. The park is most lively on weekends with performers and families.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (Line 3 to Viveros or Coyoacán station). Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly. Entry is 270 MXN (~$13 USD), which is worth every peso for its cultural significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Coyoacán neighborhood on foot — visit the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, browse the Mercado de Coyoacán for local crafts and snacks, and enjoy the colonial architecture and bohemian atmosphere. Visit the Leon Trotsky Museum nearby for 40 MXN (~$2 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the centro or stay in Coyoacán for the evening street food scene. Coyoacán's markets come alive at dusk with food stalls and artisan vendors.

meals.breakfast: Café de olla (traditional spiced coffee) and pan dulce (sweet bread) from a local panadería near the hotel — under 40 MXN (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Tostadas de tinga or memelas at Mercado de Coyoacán — authentic and incredibly cheap at 30–60 MXN (~$1.50–3 USD) per item.
meals.dinner: Pozole or enchiladas at a family-run restaurant in Coyoacán — look for a comida corrida spot for a full meal at 90–130 MXN (~$4.50–6.50 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Coyoacán is about 45 minutes from Centro by Metro — budget extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica — two of the largest and most authentic local markets in Mexico City, completely free to enter. Wander through stalls selling fresh produce, flowers, spices, and street food. A true immersion into everyday Mexico City life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec (if not visited earlier) — one of the best anthropology museums in the world with incredible Aztec, Maya, and Mesoamerican artifacts. Entry is 85 MXN (~$4 USD). Allow at least 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the city — return to Centro Histórico for a farewell walk. Visit the Zócalo one last time, pick up any last-minute souvenirs from street vendors, and enjoy a final meal at a local favorite.

meals.breakfast: Huevos rancheros or enfrijoladas at a local breakfast café near the hotel — 70–100 MXN (~$3.50–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Fresh juice, fruit cups, and antojitos (small snacks) at Mercado de la Merced — eat like a local for under 80 MXN (~$4 USD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional Mexican cantina in Centro — order mole, chiles en nogada (seasonal), or cochinita pibil with rice and beans. Budget 150–200 MXN (~$7.50–10 USD) for a full meal with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: If departing early the next day, pack bags the night before. The Metro is the cheapest way to get to the airport (Línea 5 to Terminal Aérea station) for just 5 MXN. Mexico City is generally safe in tourist areas but always stay aware of your surroundings, especially in markets.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Focus on clearing customs, collecting luggage, and arranging ground transportation to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely orientation walk around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings, locate nearby metro stations, pharmacies, and convenience stores. Visit a local mercado (market) close to the hotel to pick up snacks and get a first taste of the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the historic Centro Histórico (approximately 20–30 min by metro/taxi depending on hotel location) for a gentle first evening stroll. Admire the illuminated Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the Metropolitan Cathedral, and the Palacio Nacional exteriors. Keep it relaxed after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light bite at the airport upon arrival — try a fresh juice and tamale from an airport food stand.
meals.lunch: El Cardenal (Centro Histórico branch) — a beloved mid-range Mexican restaurant famous for traditional dishes like sopa de lima and chiles en nogada. Approx. $15–25 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Café de Tacuba — an iconic, atmospheric restaurant in Centro Histórico serving classic Mexican cuisine in a beautifully tiled colonial setting. Try the enchiladas or mole. Approx. $15–20 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Keep luggage light when heading out in the evening. Use the Metrobús or Uber for safe and affordable transport. Stay hydrated — Mexico City sits at 2,240m altitude and mild altitude fatigue is common on day one.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec. Spend 2–3 hours exploring pre-Hispanic civilizations including the iconic Aztec Sun Stone. The museum opens at 9:00 AM. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — one of the largest urban parks in the Americas. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched on the hill for panoramic views of the city and exhibits on Mexican history from the colonial era to the 20th century.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale-yet-accessible Polanco neighborhood adjacent to Chapultepec. Window-shop along Avenida Presidente Masaryk and people-watch at Parque Lincoln. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try chilaquiles (tortilla chips in salsa topped with cream and cheese) at a local fondita (small family restaurant). Approx. $5–8 USD.
meals.lunch: El Lago restaurant inside Chapultepec Park — mid-range lakeside setting with Mexican and international dishes. Great ambiance. Approx. $15–22 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Mercado de Antojitos in Polanco or Limosneros — enjoy a curated tasting of Mexican street-food-style dishes in a sit-down setting. Approx. $18–28 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo de Antropología is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with Chapultepec Castle first. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Metro Line 7 (Auditorio station) is the easiest access to Chapultepec.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — the ancient pre-Aztec city of pyramids, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City (1–1.5 hrs by bus from Terminal Central del Norte). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive by 9:00 AM to avoid midday heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the on-site Museo de Sitio. Browse local artisan stalls near the entrance for obsidian crafts and souvenirs. Return to Mexico City by mid-to-late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Recover with a relaxed evening in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood. Walk along tree-lined streets, browse independent bookshops and boutiques, and enjoy the vibrant café and bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab a torta (Mexican sandwich) or pan dulce (sweet bread) and coffee from a street stall near the bus terminal. Approx. $3–5 USD.
meals.lunch: La Gruta restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique mid-range restaurant set inside a natural cave/grotto near the archaeological site. Serves traditional Mexican cuisine. Approx. $15–25 USD per person. Book ahead if possible.
meals.dinner: Contramar or a local taquería in Roma Norte — Contramar is a beloved seafood restaurant (tuna tostadas are iconic). Mid-range pricing at approx. $20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring plenty of water for Teotihuacán — the site is largely exposed with little shade. Buses to Teotihuacán depart frequently from Terminal del Norte (Metro Autobuses del Norte, Line 5). The round trip bus fare is approximately $5–7 USD. Entrance to the site is approx. $5–7 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán — visit the vibrant Mercado de Coyoacán for fresh produce, street food, and local crafts. Then tour the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul / Blue House), the iconic home-turned-museum of the legendary Mexican painter. Book tickets online in advance as it sells out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky (former home of the exiled Russian revolutionary) for a fascinating slice of 20th-century history. Stroll through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets, visit Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, and browse independent art galleries and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a deeper evening exploration. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes (Palace of Fine Arts) to admire its stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco exterior and check if any performances or exhibitions are scheduled. Walk along Avenida Madero (pedestrian street) and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga (shredded chicken on crispy tortillas) or fresh fruit with chili and lime from market stalls. Approx. $4–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — a well-regarded mid-range restaurant with creative Mexican cuisine and excellent mezcal selection, set in a lovely courtyard. Approx. $18–28 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico in Centro Histórico — elegant yet accessible restaurant in a beautiful colonial courtyard serving refined traditional Mexican dishes. Approx. $20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked online well in advance (weeks ahead if possible) — check fridakahlo.org. Coyoacán is best reached via Metro Line 3 (Viveros or Coyoacán station) or Uber. The neighborhood has a very walkable, village-like feel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Xochimilco — a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its ancient network of canals and colorful trajineras (flat-bottomed boats). Hire a trajinera for a 1.5–2 hour canal tour, enjoy mariachi music from passing boats, and browse floating market vendors selling food, flowers, and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the neighborhood of San Ángel for a final afternoon of culture and shopping. Visit the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo (the studio-home of Diego Rivera) and browse the famous Bazar del Sábado (Saturday artisan market — if visiting on a Saturday) or the permanent craft market for unique Mexican souvenirs and handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to a favorite neighborhood (Roma Norte or Condesa recommended) for a farewell dinner. Take a last evening walk to soak in the city's energy, pick up any final souvenirs, and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Condesa or Roma café before heading to Xochimilco — try huevos rancheros (eggs in tomato-chili sauce) at a neighborhood café. Approx. $7–10 USD.
meals.lunch: Enjoy food directly on the trajinera in Xochimilco — buy quesadillas, elotes (corn on the cob), and snacks from the floating vendor boats. Budget approx. $10–15 USD for a fun, authentic floating lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Quintonil or a mid-range alternative in Polanco/Condesa — Quintonil celebrates contemporary Mexican cuisine with local ingredients (book ahead). Mid-range alternative: El Bajío in Condesa, famous for its mole and traditional recipes. Approx. $25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best reached via the Tren Ligero (light rail) from Tasqueña Metro station (Line 2) — affordable and direct. Trajinera rental costs approx. $25–40 USD per boat (shared among your group) per hour. Arrive at the embarcadero by 10:00 AM for the best experience before crowds peak. If departing Mexico City on Day 5 evening, adjust the afternoon/evening schedule accordingly to allow travel time to the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in a chauffeured Mercedes-Benz S-Class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your suite. Enjoy a welcome amenity and a relaxing orientation tour of the resort's facilities. Freshen up before heading out for a leisurely stroll through the upscale Polanco neighborhood — Mexico City's most elegant district — exploring boutique galleries, designer shops, and tree-lined boulevards.
day_by_day.evening: Private guided evening walk through Polanco, ending with cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the city skyline. Experience Mexico City's vibrant nightlife ambiance in one of its most sophisticated neighborhoods.

meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the resort's signature restaurant upon check-in — featuring contemporary Mexican cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and a curated mezcal and wine pairing menu.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol, one of Latin America's top-ranked restaurants, located steps from Polanco. Indulge in Chef Enrique Olvera's legendary tasting menu including the iconic Mole Madre — a 1,000+ day aged mole. Reservation arranged in advance by the resort concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure the resort concierge pre-books Pujol well in advance as tables are extremely limited. Private airport transfer should be confirmed before departure. Jet lag tip: stay awake until local dinner time to adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the historic Centro Histórico, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the magnificent Zócalo (main plaza), the Metropolitan Cathedral, and the Templo Mayor archaeological ruins with an expert archaeologist guide. Gain exclusive after-hours or early-access entry before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City's premier cultural landmark, admiring its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and world-class murals by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros. Continue to the nearby Museo Franz Mayer for an intimate collection of Mexican decorative arts housed in a 16th-century hospital. Private docent-led tour included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the terrace bar of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México overlooking the Zócalo — a stunning Belle Époque gem with a Tiffany stained-glass ceiling. Then transfer to dinner in the Roma Norte neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort — choose from an à la carte menu featuring fresh tropical fruits, artisan pastries, Oaxacan tlayudas, and specialty Mexican coffee from Veracruz highlands.
meals.lunch: Traditional Mexican lunch at El Cardenal, a beloved institution in the Centro Histórico renowned for its authentic regional Mexican cuisine, freshly made tortillas, and traditional hot chocolates prepared tableside.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar, an iconic Mexico City seafood institution in Colonia Roma. Savor the legendary tuna tostadas, whole grilled fish with two salsas, and a curated selection of natural wines and craft cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Centro Histórico tour. The area can be busy mid-morning — early arrival is recommended. The resort concierge can arrange all private guides and museum entry in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city located approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Arrive early for a VIP sunrise experience atop the Pyramid of the Sun before general tourists arrive. A private archaeologist guide will provide an in-depth narrative of this extraordinary UNESCO site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Pyramid of the Moon, the Avenue of the Dead, and the stunning murals of the Palace of Tepantitla. Enjoy a private al fresco lunch within the archaeological zone with panoramic views of the pyramids. On the return journey, stop at a renowned artisan workshop in San Juan Teotihuacán to observe and purchase obsidian crafts and traditional textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a traditional temazcal (pre-Hispanic steam ceremony) experience at the resort spa, followed by a soothing massage using indigenous Mexican botanicals and techniques.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort (pre-packed gourmet basket option available for the early departure) — featuring pan dulce, fresh fruit, and thermos of premium Mexican coffee.
meals.lunch: Private catered gourmet lunch at Teotihuacán — a curated spread of traditional Mexican dishes including slow-cooked lamb barbacoa, handmade tortillas, guacamole, and fresh agua frescas served with a view of the pyramids.
meals.dinner: In-room or resort restaurant dining after the spa experience. Opt for the resort's curated 'Flavors of Mexico' tasting menu featuring dishes inspired by regional Mexican states, paired with artisanal mezcals.

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 6:00 AM for the sunrise experience at Teotihuacán. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable athletic shoes — the pyramid climb is moderately strenuous. The temazcal ceremony should be booked through the resort spa at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive culinary experience: a private market tour and hands-on cooking class with a Michelin-recognized chef. Begin at Mercado de Medellín or Mercado Jamaica — two of Mexico City's most vibrant and authentic local markets — selecting fresh ingredients, exotic chiles, heirloom corn, and tropical produce. Learn about the cultural and historical significance of Mexican ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the cooking masterclass in a beautifully appointed private kitchen studio in Colonia Roma. Learn to prepare three to four iconic Mexican dishes — such as mole negro, chiles en nogada, ceviche de camarón, and traditional churros with artisan chocolate sauce. Enjoy the meal you've prepared with wine or mezcal pairings.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the bohemian and artistic neighborhood of Coyoacán — home of Frida Kahlo. Explore the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) with a private after-hours exclusive access tour, experiencing the artist's home and personal collection without the daytime crowds. Stroll through Coyoacán's charming colonial plazas and artisan market.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — indulge in chilaquiles rojos with organic eggs, handmade blue corn tortillas, fresh-squeezed juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class serve as an elaborate and memorable lunch experience — a truly unique farm-to-table moment.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil, Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant in Polanco, consistently ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants. The tasting menu highlights hyper-local Mexican ingredients and indigenous techniques reimagined with modern elegance.

day_by_day.notes: The Frida Kahlo Museum private after-hours access must be arranged well in advance through a premium tour operator or the resort concierge — standard public tickets sell out weeks ahead. The cooking class can be tailored to dietary preferences upon request.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at the resort. Enjoy a spa treatment or a peaceful breakfast on your private terrace. Visit the Museo Soumaya in Polanco — a striking silver-façade architectural marvel housing one of Mexico's most impressive private art collections, including works by Rodin, Dalí, Monet, and a vast collection of Mexican and Latin American masters. Private guided tour arranged.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping experience in Polanco and the Masaryk Avenue corridor — Mexico City's equivalent of the Champs-Élysées. Browse flagship boutiques of international luxury brands alongside acclaimed Mexican designers such as Pineda Covalín. Visit Mercado Artz or a curated artisan gallery to select premium Mexican crafts, Talavera ceramics, and fine silver jewelry as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner at a world-class restaurant. Departure preparations — the resort concierge arranges a luxury private transfer to the airport. Final cocktails at the resort bar toasting to an extraordinary Mexico City experience.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the resort — champagne brunch option with a full spread of Mexican and international favorites, fresh pastries, smoked fish, artisan cheeses, and tropical fruit platters.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rosetta, Chef Elena Reygadas' iconic restaurant in Colonia Roma, renowned for its Italian-influenced Mexican cuisine, house-baked bread, and elegant garden setting. A must-visit for food lovers.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Dulce Patria in Polanco, Chef Martha Ortiz's celebrated culinary theater where Mexican tradition meets high gastronomy. The dramatic presentation and bold flavors make for an unforgettable final evening. Pair with a flight of premium tequila añejo selections.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours prior to scheduled departure. Allow time for luggage packing and checkout procedures. The resort concierge can assist with shipping any larger souvenir purchases home. Ensure all restaurant reservations for this final day are reconfirmed the morning of.
